title: Launch Console
setting: Rocket Propulsion Test Stand & Firing Room, including the indoor Launch & Static Test Firing Room and High-Bay Vehicle Integration Cleanroom & Test Cell, with stations at the Firing Console, Fluid & Calibration Bench, High-Bay Integration Staging Bay, Fluid Management Manifold, Static Test Stand, and Launch Director Podium
rules: Launch Commit Criteria (LCC) are Absolute: Every engine redline has hard limits defined before propellant loading; if any parameter drifts outside during terminal countdown, an immediate hold or auto-abort must be initiated
Stoichiometry Dictates Survival: Propellant mixture ratios are deliberately tuned off-stoichiometric (fuel-rich) to preserve combustion chamber wall integrity against temperatures exceeding 3,500 K
Prevent Hard Starts at All Costs: Propellant must never accumulate in the thrust chamber prior to ignition, as liquid oxygen and hydrocarbon fuel pooling leads to chamber detonations

Failsafe Redundancy & Triage: Hardware failures are classified strictly according to standard hazard severity tables (MIL-STD-882E / NASA-STD-8729.1), and single-point failures on critical systems require an immediate mission scrub
Traceability & Chain of Custody: Flight hardware, safety pins, and ordnance must have serialized sign-offs, and no unauthorized tool or component can remain inside the vehicle envelope
assumptions: The vehicle modeled uses a standard bipropellant liquid rocket engine (LOX oxidizer and RP-1 kerosene fuel) operating with a gas-generator or expander cycle
The engineer acts as the Propulsion Operations & Systems Lead, transitioning from pre-fire configuration to countdown command

tasks.title: Calibrate engine fluid ratios
tasks.summary: Configure the engine controller's primary hydraulic variables at the Fluid & Calibration Bench, including the oxidizer-to-fuel mass ratio, chamber pressure, injector pressure drop ratio, and fuel film-cooling bypass percentage before a hot-fire test.
tasks.mechanic_rationale: The mix mechanic accurately models the independent numeric tuning across interconnected continuous fluid parameters with narrow tolerance margins.
tasks.aim: Calibrate the hydraulic regulators, trim valves, and cooling bypass on the test bench to establish a stable and safe engine operating envelope before hot-fire testing.

optima.rationale: Running fuel-rich lowers combustion gas molecular weight, maximizes characteristic velocity and specific impulse, and limits flame temperature to manageable levels below 3500 K.
Sizing chamber pressure at 70 bar establishes required thrust and throat mass flux while providing optimal sea-level nozzle expansion without internal shock separation.
A pressure drop ratio between 15% and 20% decouples the propellant feed system from combustion chamber acoustic oscillations, avoiding low-frequency instabilities.
Allocating 3.5% to 5.0% of fuel to peripheral film cooling creates a protective boundary sub-layer that insulates the chamber liner without excessive specific impulse loss.
The resulting differential pressure across the injector must remain between 10.20 bar and 14.40 bar to maintain acoustic decoupling without exceeding pump delivery limits.
Accounting for film cooling diversion, the core combustion zone ratio must remain between 2.38 and 2.63 to avoid elevating core gas temperatures by over 250 K.

heuristic.too_low: Incomplete combustion produces soot and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, showing an opaque, orange, smoky exhaust plume and fouling cooling channels.
heuristic.too_high: Excess free oxygen creates an aggressive oxidizing environment and elevated flame temperatures, causing chamber liner oxidation and throat erosion.
heuristic.rationale: Deviating from optimal O/F either causes incomplete combustion fouling or aggressive thermal and oxidative attack on copper liners.

heuristic.too_low: Nozzle exit pressure drops below ambient limits, causing asymmetric flow separation, dangerous side loads, and nozzle skirt flutter.
heuristic.too_high: Convective heat flux scales aggressively, threatening liner burn-through and exceeding structural hoop stress safety margins.
heuristic.rationale: Chamber pressure governs nozzle expansion dynamics and structural heat flux loads.

heuristic.too_low: Combustion noise couples with feedline elasticity, triggering low-frequency chugging instability and violent thrust oscillations.
heuristic.too_high: Excessive upstream feed pressure is demanded, increasing turbopump cavitation risk, while atomization overshoot splatters liquid on the injector face.
heuristic.rationale: Injector pressure drop ratio serves as an acoustic barrier isolating the feed lines from chamber acoustics.

heuristic.too_low: Thermal boundary layer breaks down, causing liner blanching, thermal fatigue cracking, and hot gas burnout near the throat.
heuristic.too_high: Specific impulse degrades substantially, with unburned fuel streaking down the nozzle to form heavy coking deposits and hydrocarbon smoke.
heuristic.rationale: BFC bypass balances thermal liner protection against performance loss and soot deposition.

heuristic.too_low: Manifold pressure differential is insufficient, nearing the bench abort interlock due to lack of hydraulic acoustic isolation.
heuristic.too_high: Manifold back-pressure approaches supply limits, overloading feed components.
heuristic.rationale: Absolute injector drop must ensure acoustic stability without exceeding turbopump discharge limits.

heuristic.too_low: Core combustion runs excessively fuel-rich, quenching core efficiency and degrading combustion stability.
heuristic.too_high: Core zone temperatures rise drastically, accelerating throat erosion even with peripheral cooling active.
heuristic.rationale: Core mixture ratio directly drives local core gas temperatures and chamber throat life.

caveats: Volumetric flow calibration must be compensated against RTD temperature telemetry before setting mass mixture ratios due to cryogenic LOX density swings with chill-down temperature and subcooling.
Calibrated steady-state O/F must not be applied prior to ignition; injector calibration benches must enforce a 20 to 50 ms fuel-lead pre-injection sequence to avoid explosive hard starts.
Upstream cavitating venturis must maintain a pressure recovery drop of at least 15% across their throats to prevent chamber pressure fluctuations from feeding back to main propellant tanks.
problems: Low-frequency pressure oscillations (100–300 Hz chugging) occurring when injector pressure drop ratio falls below 15.0% of chamber pressure.
Local wall blanching and copper discoloration near the chamber throat when barrier film cooling bypass drops below 3.5% or suffers circumferential maldistribution.
Heavy soot deposits, sluggish ignition ramp, and low characteristic velocity efficiency when O/F is below 2.30 or BFC bypass exceeds 5.0%.
Excessive manifold back-pressure exceeding pump discharge limits (> 85 bar) when injector pressure drop ratio exceeds 20.0%.

tasks.title: Time chilldown and ignition
tasks.summary: Execute the automated terminal countdown sequence at the Firing Console by timing the cryogenic line chilldown bleed, initiating the TEA-TEB pyrophoric igniter torch, and holding the chamber throttle ramp to mainstage.
tasks.mechanic_rationale: The timing mechanic mirrors the time-critical transient phases of a rocket engine start sequence via dynamic hold and stop actions on moving countdown indicators.
tasks.aim: Execute the terminal countdown sequence by precisely timing cryogenic chilldown, pyrophoric igniter injection lead, and intermediate thrust ramp dwell.

optima.rationale: Allows LOX feedlines and turbopump housings to transition past film boiling to dense liquid conditions while avoiding excess cryogen boil-off or structural frost accumulation.
Establishes a stable TEA-TEB radical flame kernel just before main propellant admission without risking hard starts from delayed ignition or orifice slagging from unbacked burning.

Ensures chamber acoustic flame anchoring and turbopump power stabilization at intermediate plateau pressure before spooling to full thrust, preventing chug instability or regenerative throat overheating.

heuristic.too_low: Cryogenic lines exhibit two-phase film boiling, causing erratic manifold pressure oscillations and turbopump cavitation from insufficient liquid density.
heuristic.too_high: Excessive overboard cryogen expenditure leads to ullage collapse, external manifold frost accumulation, and low-temperature valve freeze alarms.
heuristic.rationale: Chilldown must clear the Leidenfrost regime without wasting propellant margins or freezing valve seals.

heuristic.too_low: Hypergolic ignition slug arrives late, causing unignited propellants to pool and detonate in a destructive high-pressure hard start.
heuristic.too_high: Pyrophoric torch burns out prematurely without propellant backing, forming solid oxide slag deposits that plug injector micro-orifices.
heuristic.rationale: Pyrophoric lead time governs whether propellant mixes into an existing flame or accumulates into an explosive acoustic pulse.

heuristic.too_low: Chamber flame anchoring fails to stabilize, driving severe acoustic chug or screech instabilities and turbine inlet temperature spikes during ramp.
heuristic.too_high: Low-flow intermediate dwell exposes nozzle throat liners to high thermal flux without sufficient coolant velocity, triggering overheat alarms and sequencer timeout.
heuristic.rationale: Dwell time at intermediate thrust balances acoustic anchoring against cooling channel heat capacity.

caveats: Liquid oxygen contacts ambient walls initially in the film boiling regime; main oxidizer valves must not open while feedline skin thermocouples indicate transition temperatures above 95 K [10].
TEA-TEB pyrophoric fluid decomposes spontaneously on contact with air or moisture; manifolds must maintain a dry GN2 blanket (> 50 psig) until firing [2, 21, 28].
Lead intervals between igniter discharge and main valve actuation must cushion hydraulic water hammer against downstream chamber backpressure [7, 15, 18, 29].
problems: Cryogenic Vapor Lock / Turbopump Cavitation: Caused by Phase 1 duration < 3.5 s; manifests as high-frequency discharge pressure oscillations (100–300 Hz) and rapid drop in oxidizer mass flow [5, 10, 25].
Combustor Hard Start Detonation: Caused by Phase 2 lead < 120 ms; manifests as destructive dynamic pressure pulse exceeding 2.5x rated chamber pressure and acoustic accelerometer trips [13, 20].
Igniter Injector Coking & Vitreous Slagging: Caused by Phase 2 lead > 180 ms; manifests as TEA-TEB differential pressure rising > 20% and dimmed optical detector output [13, 21].
Start-Transient Chug / Screech Instability: Caused by Phase 3 dwell < 1.8 s; manifests as low-frequency (50–150 Hz) or high-frequency (> 1500 Hz) chamber pressure hum [10, 15, 24].
Regenerative Throat Overheat: Caused by Phase 3 dwell > 2.2 s; manifests as nozzle throat wall temperature gradient exceeding 80 K/s and coolant delta-T exceeding limits [15].

tasks.title: Triage telemetry hazard warnings
tasks.summary: Sort live sensor redline exceedances, telemetry anomalies, and fault logs into four system safety hazard categories at the Firing Console during hot-fire processing.
tasks.mechanic_rationale: The sort mechanic models categorizing an incoming stream of operational events into standardized regulatory bins.
tasks.aim: Route live telemetry redline exceedances, sensor anomalies, and test stand fault logs into their correct system safety hazard severity categories during a rocket engine hot-fire test.

sort_items.label: ITEM_HPOTP_VIB: HPOTP bearing radial accelerometer VIB-OX-104A at 22.4 g RMS sustained for 65 ms (Redline: > 18.0 g RMS for > 50 ms)
sort_items.feedback: HPOTP bearing raceway spallation or rubbing in a 100% supercritical LOX stream leads to frictional ignition and uncontained turbopump structural disintegration, resulting in total loss of engine and test stand asset (monetary loss >= $10M).

sort_items.label: ITEM_MCC_DP_DROP: MCC coolant jacket differential pressure MCC-DP-201B drops to 380 psid (Redline: < 450 psid) with throat skin temp TC-THRT-209 exceeding 1,150 K
sort_items.feedback: Coolant flow collapse leads to instantaneous throat wall thermal erosion and high-pressure chamber rupture at high heat fluxes, destroying the thrust frame and facility (monetary loss >= $10M).

sort_items.label: ITEM_TVC_HYD_LOSS: Primary gimbal actuator TVC supply pressure HYD-P-302 drops to 1,720 psia (Redline abort: < 2,100 psia for > 100 ms) with actuator servo stall warning
sort_items.feedback: Loss of gimbal actuator authority prevents thrust vectoring, aborting primary test and flight certification objectives and requiring major component requalification ($1M to $10M loss), but the engine remains physically contained on the stand.

sort_items.label: ITEM_PB_SEAL_LEAK: Preburner dual seal cavity purge pressure PRG-P-405 rises to 58 psia (Warning threshold: 45 psia) with leak rate at 140 sccm
sort_items.feedback: Secondary containment seal leak vents propellant into an inert GN2 buffer without cross-over, causing minor mission degradation (truncating test duration by 30 seconds) and minor teardown repairs ($100k to $1M loss).

sort_items.label: ITEM_DELUGE_FLOW_DIP: Flame trench acoustic water deluge manifold FAC-FLW-501 drops to 36,500 GPM (Minimum specification: 41,000 GPM) for 1.8 s
sort_items.feedback: Deluge flow dip degrades acoustic and thermal mitigation, causing localized concrete spalling and deflector plate fatigue needing minor stand repairs and 3 days of downtime ($100k to $1M loss).

sort_items.label: ITEM_STRUCT_TC_OPEN: Structural mast ambient skin thermocouple TC-SKIN-608D reports open circuit (9,999 °C / NaN flag) while redundant channels A, B, and C report 21 °C
sort_items.feedback: Open-circuit failure on a non-controlling channel with redundant sensors reporting nominal conditions causes no hardware damage or mission degradation, requiring only routine post-test cable replacement (< $100k loss).

caveats: Never categorize hazard severity based on a raw single-channel spike unless verified against physical voting logic or companion parameters (e.g., pairing turbopump vibration with bearing cavity temperature).
Account for sensor persistence windows (30 to 50 ms) to avoid misclassifying sub-10 ms electrical transients or inductive kicks as catastrophic events.

Hazard classification varies by operational environment: flight critical failure modes (e.g., loss of TVC causing loss of vehicle) are Category I in flight but classified as Category II on a bolted ground test stand.
problems: Cryogenic chilldown sensor bias shift: Pressure transducers experience zero-shift drift of 8 to 12 psia at cryogenic temperatures (< -180 °C), tripping false low-pressure warnings at ignition.
Two-phase flow noise tripping purge monitors: Boil-off expansion during startup transients causes purge cavity pressure spikes (> 50 psia) between T0 and T+2.5 s.
Flame deflector water steam ingress: Trench water mist penetrates sensor connectors, producing high-frequency electrical noise (> 25 g at 10 kHz) that mimics bearing failure.

tasks.title: Answer readiness poll questions
tasks.summary: Respond across the mission intercom loop at the Launch Director Podium during the formal terminal countdown Go/No-Go readiness poll at T-9 minutes.
tasks.mechanic_rationale: The converse mechanic models multi-turn intercom communication where every response must adhere strictly to established engineering flight rules.
tasks.aim: Certify vehicle cryogenic conditioning, launch commit criteria, and voice loop readiness status as PROP during a terminal countdown poll.

dialogue.npc_line: PROP, this is LD on Countdown Net 1. Verify stage-one LOX engine chilldown and subcooling purge status at the T-9 minute hold.

options.text: LD, PROP. LOX pump bleeds verified at -184.2 °C, within the subcooling threshold below -183 °C. GHe purge hold sequence complete, engine manifold temperatures are stable and conditioned.
options.feedback: Precise, standard callsign discipline citing physical telemetry verified below the subcooling threshold and confirming completion of the moisture purge sequence.

options.text: LD, PROP. Chilldown is progressing well; bleeds are hovering right around -180 °C, which is close enough to liquid saturation, and the purge is actively flowing.
options.feedback: -180 °C is above the atmospheric boiling point of liquid oxygen (-182.96 °C), meaning two-phase boiling and vapor cavities exist that could cause turbopump cavitation.

options.text: LD, PROP. We have a transient manifold bleed spike up to -174 °C, but once the turbopump pre-valves open during the terminal count, bulk LOX flow will chill it down before ignition. We are good to continue.
options.feedback: Violates Launch Commit Criteria. Initiating sequence into an unconditioned cryogenic state can result in vapor lock and catastrophic turbopump destruction.

options.text: Yeah, Launch Director, PROP here. My screens are showing green on the temperatures and the purge seems active on the board.
options.feedback: Violates loop protocol through informal colloquial phrasing, vague impressions, and an absence of engineering units or telemetry verification.

dialogue.npc_line: Weather and PROP, LD. Tactical radar paints an isolated, non-transparent cumulus cell 8 nautical miles west of our flight corridor with tops measured at the -22 °C isotherm level. PROP, evaluate impact to launch commit under Lightning Launch Commit Criteria.

options.text: LD, PROP. Red constraint under LLCC Rule G417.7. Slant distance is 8 nautical miles, violating the mandatory 10-nautical-mile standoff for cumulus tops colder than -20 °C. PROP is NO-GO on weather.
options.feedback: Correctly applies standard Lightning Launch Commit Criteria requiring a 10-nautical-mile standoff from cumulus clouds colder than -20 °C and issues a clear NO-GO.

options.text: LD, PROP. The cumulus cell is 8 nautical miles out and drifting west away from the pad. Because the flight path does not physically penetrate the cloud envelope, PROP recommends we waive the rule and declare GO.
options.feedback: Violates safety criteria by attempting an unauthorized waiver. Triggered lightning does not require flying through the cloud to initiate an electrical discharge.

options.text: LD, PROP. That cloud is close at 8 nautical miles, but if the surface electric field mills read below 1 kilovolt per meter, we might have an exception. Let's ask Weather to check the field mill network before we hold.
options.feedback: Misapplies field mill exceptions, which do not apply to cumulus cloud tops colder than -20 °C.

options.text: LD, PROP. 8 nautical miles is within the 10-mile circle. That doesn't look compliant, so we probably need to hold, but I defer entirely to the Weather Officer.
options.feedback: Indecisive and passive response. Every console polled must directly assert safety criteria affecting the vehicle and deliver an unambiguous call.

dialogue.npc_line: Copy, holding at T-9 minutes. Weather confirms the cumulus cell has fully collapsed to +8 °C and dissipated. However, the pad anemometer at the 162-foot level reports sustained winds of 26 knots, with peak gusts recorded at 36 knots. PROP, evaluate umbilical release and tail-service mast clearance for terminal count entry.

options.text: LD, PROP. Peak gusts of 36 knots violate our structural and umbilical commit limit of 30 knots sustained, 33 knots peak gust. PROP recommends holding until peak gusts remain under 30 knots for 10 consecutive minutes.
options.feedback: Correctly identifies that a 36-knot gust violates structural and umbilical release thresholds and appropriately requests a consecutive stabilization window.

options.text: LD, PROP. Sustained wind is 26 knots, which is technically under our 30-knot sustained limit. The 36-knot gusts are brief transients, so we can pick up the count and rely on the automatic ground sequencer to abort if a gust hits at T-10 seconds.
options.feedback: Flawed operational risk practice. Countdowns should not proceed into known violating gusts relying solely on terminal automatic redline aborts.

options.text: LD, PROP. High gusts actually improve hydrogen dispersion at the tail service mast. 36 knots is well within vehicle flight aerodynamic limits, so PROP is GO to resume.
options.feedback: Conflates in-flight aerodynamic parameters with pad structural hold-down loads and ground umbilical disconnect envelopes.

options.text: LD, PROP. Can we ask the MET team to determine if that 36-knot gust was a one-second spike or a three-second average before we decide whether to hold?
options.feedback: Introduces unnecessary net debate; Launch Commit Criteria peak gusts refer to peak instantaneous readings across anemometer arrays.

dialogue.npc_line: Wind has moderated to 20 knots sustained, peak gusts 24 knots over the last 15 minutes. All Lightning Launch Commit Criteria are green. Cryogenic systems are replenished and stable. We are polling to resume count and enter terminal sequencing at T-9 minutes. PROP, your status?

options.text: LD, PROP is GO to resume countdown and enter terminal sequence.
options.feedback: Standard, concise operational protocol identifying station, addressee, and explicit GO status for the planned terminal action.

options.text: PROP is ready. Pressures and temperatures are all looking good on my telemetry displays; go ahead and pick up the count whenever the rest of the team is ready.
options.feedback: Informal and verbose response that omits the standard canonical keyword 'GO'.

options.text: LD, PROP is NO-GO... wait, sorry, re-checking sensor PT-401... bleeds warmed up to -182.8 °C, but that's within 0.2 degrees of the limit. Scratch that, PROP is GO, let's roll.
options.feedback: Vacillating between NO-GO and GO, guessing near limit margins, and using unprofessional slang on a formal terminal poll triggers mandatory holds and investigations.

options.text: Launch Director, this is the Propulsion Systems Console Lead speaking. The engineering support team in the back room has completed our review and we concur with resuming count.
options.feedback: Excessively wordy and non-standard callsign usage consumes critical countdown voice net time.

caveats: LOX boils at -182.96 °C (90.19 K) at standard atmospheric pressure; subcooling to temperatures below -183 °C is essential to avoid turbopump cavitation.
Engine turbopump bearings and fuel injectors require positive-pressure purge conditioning (typically > 1.2 bar absolute) to avoid icing and atmospheric condensation prior to chilldown.
Under LLCC (14 CFR Appendix G to Part 417), cumulus clouds with tops colder than -20 °C require a strict 10-nautical-mile standoff from the flight path.

Field mill exemptions apply only to warm non-precipitating cumulus regimes between +5 °C and -5 °C (or specific -10 °C regimes) under strict electric field limits, never to cloud tops colder than -20 °C.
Ground wind limits at the 162-foot level are typically capped at 30 knots sustained and 33 to 34 knots peak gust to prevent excessive bending moments and umbilical re-contact.
problems: Extended hold times lead to passive heat soak into chilldown bleeds, requiring a propellant replenish or bleed recirculation rate increase to restore subcooling below -183 °C.
Distant cumulus tops crossing -20 °C within 10 nautical miles create lightning trigger risks that require an immediate NO-GO rather than relying on visual pad observations.
Intermittent wind gusts breaching 33 to 34 knots require declaring a HOLD and observing a mandatory clear window (e.g., 10 minutes) below limits.
Net clutter and informal phrasing degrade situational awareness; operators must strictly follow standard station callouts and concise status declarations.

tasks.title: Deliver safety arming hardware
tasks.summary: Transport serialized mechanical safe-and-arm lockout pins, transducer cal-plugs, and ground lanyards from the High-Bay Integration Staging Bay to the test stand and pad interface before pad clearance lockouts.
tasks.mechanic_rationale: The deliver mechanic simulates moving delicate safety-critical items across cleanroom and pad waypoints within a strict countdown time constraint.
tasks.aim: Transport and deliver safety lockout, shunt calibration, and grounding hardware from the staging cleanroom to designated thrust stand interfaces within pad clearance time limits.

orders.item: Serialized Detent Safe-and-Arm Lockout Pin (P/N SA-PIN-417, S/N 019)
orders.destination: Lead Ordnance Engineer at Thrust Mount S&A Bracket (Target ID: TM-SA-01)
orders.note: Priority 1. Carry in conductive, padded sleeve with under 15 g transverse shock. Deliver within 20 s to verify detent seating before pad clearance siren.

orders.item: Serialized Precision Resistive Shunt Calibration Dummy Plug (P/N CAL-PLUG-100K-B, S/N 084)
orders.destination: Instrumentation Specialist at Stand Junction Box J-04 (Target ID: TB-JB-04)
orders.note: Priority 2. Class 1A ESD sensitive (< 250 V); require anti-static strap and protective ESD conductive caps. Deliver within 35 s.

orders.item: Serialized Braided Copper-Beryllium Static Grounding Lanyard with Quick-Disconnect Clamp (P/N BND-LNYD-08, S/N 112)
orders.destination: Mechanical Integration Technician at Engine Gimbal Pad Interface (Target ID: TM-GMB-GND)
orders.note: Priority 3. Avoid kinking and shield clamp teeth from grit/oil to ensure < 2.5 mΩ bonding. Deliver within 45 s before airlock seals.

caveats: All safety arming and calibration hardware must be transported and secured across the transit corridor within a strict 45-second deadline before pad clearance lockouts seal the area and arm deluge/purge interlocks.

Never force or hammer a stuck S&A lockout pin; if insertion force exceeds 22 N (5 lbf), check the optical indicator to confirm the hard-mechanical SAFE position (90° out-of-line) and use a cleanroom micro-alignment tool.
Range safety regulations strictly prohibit straightening bent connector pins on safety-critical instrumentation connectors; bent pins must be tagged out and replaced.
Differential pressure across the cleanroom airlock must not exceed 50 Pa (0.20 in. H2O); verify the green differential pressure indicator LED before entering to avoid seal interlock lockouts.
problems: Pin detent jamming stopping 10 mm short of full insertion caused by thermal expansion mismatch, rotor misalignment, or galling/corrosion of internal spring detent balls.
Bonding resistance exceeding 2.5 mΩ threshold due to anodized coatings, primer overspray, oxidation, or dirty clamp teeth.
Transducer calibration signal baseline offset fluctuations (> 0.05 mV/V) caused by bent pins or gold-plating wear from misaligned connector mating.
Courier trapped at integration airlock doors when differential pressure exceeds 50 Pa, requiring manual bypass dump valve operation.
